data.body_html:
Cabopino dolphin watching morning vs afternoon Marbella – which time slot delivers the best experience? The answer depends on your priorities: calm seas and golden light in the morning, or warmer water and active dolphins in the afternoon. Both options depart from Puerto Banús, just 5 nautical miles from the dolphin-rich waters off Cabopino. Whether you choose a 2-hour sprint or an 8-hour cruise, your charter includes a licensed skipper, drinks, snacks, and insurance. Let’s break down the differences so you can book the perfect slot.

Why Cabopino is a dolphin hotspot

Cabopino, a small marina east of Marbella, sits near the Río Verde estuary. Nutrient-rich currents attract baitfish, which in turn draw bottlenose and striped dolphins year-round. The area’s moderate depth (15–30 m) and clear water make sightings reliable, especially between May and October when sea temperatures range from 18°C to 26°C. Morning tours benefit from less boat traffic, while afternoon trips enjoy warmer surface layers that often trigger feeding frenzies.

Morning tours: calm seas and sharp light

Morning charters (typically 9:00–11:00) offer the flattest sea conditions. The Levante wind usually picks up after midday, so early departures mean less rocking – ideal for families with young children or anyone prone to seasickness. The low-angle sun creates excellent photo conditions, illuminating dolphin dorsal fins against deep blue water. Our Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are perfect for small groups. At €749 for 2 hours, you get a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks included.

Morning tours also allow you to combine dolphin watching with a swim stop at Cala del Faro before the crowds arrive. If you’re on an 8-hour charter (€2,299), you can cruise east to Marbella Marina for lunch.

Afternoon tours: warmer water and active dolphins

Afternoon departures (15:00–17:00) coincide with peak dolphin activity. As the sea warms, dolphins often hunt closer to the surface, making them easier to spot. The golden hour light (18:00–20:00) paints the La Concha mountain in warm hues – a photographer’s dream. Our Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski, perfect for adrenaline after dolphin watching. Minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719.

Afternoon tours are also popular for sunset cruises. After spotting dolphins off Cabopino, anchor near Cala Cortés for a swim, then watch the sun dip behind the Golden Mile. The Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) and Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) are excellent choices for a stylish afternoon outing.

Both time slots offer reliable sightings, but the choice comes down to your group’s preferences. For a detailed overview of all our boats, visit our boat rental Marbella page.

Which boat should you book?

For a 2-hour dolphin-watching trip, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both Tier A at €749) are cost-effective. For a full-day adventure, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers a spacious flybridge for panoramic dolphin spotting. If you want luxury, the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) provides a sundeck and jacuzzi – perfect for afternoon charters. All bookings include skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks. See our full fleet for pricing and availability.

Practical tips for your trip

  • Book ahead – summer slots fill quickly, especially weekends.
  • Arrive 15 minutes early at Puerto Banús for boarding.
  • Bring sunscreen – even morning sun reflects off the water.
  • Pack a light jacket – morning sea breezes can be cool.
  • Ask your skipper – they know the best dolphin zones and can adjust the route.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best time of day for Cabopino dolphin watching?

Morning tours (9:00–11:00) offer flat seas and good light for photography. Afternoon tours (15:00–17:00) have warmer water and often higher dolphin activity. Both times yield reliable sightings, but mornings are preferred for families with young children.

How long does a dolphin-watching tour from Puerto Banús take?

A typical dolphin-watching trip to Cabopino lasts 2 hours. For a more relaxed experience, book a 4-hour or 8-hour charter that includes swimming stops at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. The 2-hour option costs €749 on Tier A boats.

Which boats are best for dolphin watching?

The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal for small groups. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers a flybridge with panoramic views. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.

Are dolphin sightings guaranteed?

No charter can guarantee wildlife sightings, but the waters off Cabopino have a 90%+ sighting rate from May to October. Common species include bottlenose and striped dolphins. If you don't see dolphins, you still enjoy the Costa del Sol coastline.

What is included in the charter price?

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs.

Can I combine dolphin watching with other activities?

Yes. An 8-hour charter (€2,299 on Tier A boats) lets you visit Cabopino dolphin zone, swim at Cala del Faro, anchor near La Concha, and enjoy lunch at a chiringuito. The Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski for extra fun.

What should I bring for a dolphin-watching trip?

Bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, sunglasses, a light jacket for morning wind, and a camera. The boat provides towels, drinks, and snacks. For afternoon trips, consider a swimsuit for a dip.
